info.name: Super Karigar — Worker App API (v1)
info.description:
Token-based (Sanctum) JSON API for the Super Karigar worker mobile app.

Quick start:
1. Set the `base_url` collection variable (default http://localhost:8000).
2. Run **Auth → Send OTP**, then check storage/logs for the dev OTP.
3. Run **Auth → Verify OTP** — it auto-saves the returned token into the `token` variable, so every other request is authenticated.

Full reference: docs/worker-app-api.md
KYC, DigiLocker and instant verification: docs/kyc-verification-decentro.md

request.description: Send/resend a 4-digit OTP. In dev (no MSG91 keys) the code is written to storage/logs.
Verify OTP → issue token (auto-registers on first login). The test script stores the token in the collection variable.
Permanently delete the account (revokes all tokens). Requires confirm=true.
States, skills, spoken languages, education levels, wage types, app languages, job categories.

request.description:
Send any subset of fields. The signup wizard calls this per step.

`area` is the karigar's locality; employers see "2.3 km · T. Nagar, Chennai". Send `latitude`/`longitude` only when the karigar sets their location: with `location_source: gps` (phone; the server names the area) or `area` (a place picked from Search places, sent with its `area`). An `area` alone is looked up; a new city alone moves the pin to the city centre. See docs/worker-app-api.md "Where the karigar is".
Attach an image file (≤2 MB) to the `avatar` form field.

item.name: Resume
item.description: Worker resume upload. The AI matcher reads the resume text when scoring a new application, so it directly affects the match score the employer sees. The AI resume builder (form → AI draft → edit → save) makes the resume PDF for a karigar who has none.

request.description: Current resume metadata, or `{ "resume": null }` when none is uploaded.

Attach a **PDF** (≤4 MB) to the `resume` form field. Replaces any existing resume. Returns 422 if the file is not a PDF or has no readable text layer (a scan/photo saved as PDF). The extracted text feeds the AI match score.
Removes the PDF and its extracted text; later applications are scored on the profile alone.
The resume PDF itself (uploaded or made in the AI builder), `application/pdf`. 404 when there is none.

request.description: Search box of the "Show jobs near" sheet. A city name ("jaip", "Udaipur, Tri") is answered at once from our own list; a locality, PIN code or Hindi text goes to OpenStreetMap (about a second the first time). Call it on Search or after ~400 ms without typing, never on every key (30/minute per user).

Feed around a place from **Search places** (send its latitude, longitude and label) or a pin dropped on the map (no label: the server names it, about a second slower). The answer carries `jobs`: the feed's first page around the new place, exactly what `GET /jobs` returns, so show it without calling `GET /jobs` again. Its `links.next` points at `GET /jobs`. Optional `all: true` for all categories. Spec: docs/worker-app-feed-location.md

query.description: The phone's position, for the jobs sent back

request.description: Back to "my current location". Send the phone's `lat` / `lng` to get the feed's first page around it back in `jobs` (same shape as `GET /jobs`). Optional `all=1` for all categories.
The karigar's feed: their categories, nearest first from lat/lng (the phone's position). Any of q/state/city/category/skill switches to the full search; all=1 drops the category filter.

`meta.can_apply`: the job is open and you have not applied. `meta.verification.can_apply`: whether the karigar's KYC lets them apply. When it is false, show `meta.verification.message` and **Complete KYC** instead of **Apply**.

While the admin rule is on, a karigar without a verified KYC gets `422` with `code: "verification_required"` and a `verification` block: show `message` and a **Complete KYC** button. Other 422s: already applied, and `code: "job_not_hiring"` (paused job).

request.description: `kyc` (null until submitted), `required_documents`, `digilocker` (`available`, `verified`, `name`, `masked_aadhaar`), `auto_verification_enabled`, and `verification` (`can_apply` + `message` for the apply button). Each `kyc.documents[]` entry has a `check` with what the automatic lookup found (`null` = not checked automatically).

request.description:
Starts an Aadhaar check through DigiLocker and saves `reference` into `{{kyc_reference}}`. Open `authorization_url` in a Custom Tab / SFSafariViewController / WebView, where the karigar signs in to DigiLocker with their Aadhaar OTP. Close the browser once its URL starts with `return_url_prefix`, then call **DigiLocker result**. The session lasts `expires_in_minutes` (60).

`422 digilocker_unavailable`: the admin switched auto-verify off, so fall back to typing the Aadhaar number. Limit 10/hour.

response.name: 422 · auto-verify switched off

request.description: How the DigiLocker attempt in `{{kyc_reference}}` went: `initiated` (not back yet), `passed`, `invalid` or `error` (show `message`). `kyc` comes along, because finishing DigiLocker can verify a submission that was waiting for review.

The saved examples were recorded against a test registry. The numbers in the bodies are placeholders, so the real registry answers `422 "not found"` to them: use real numbers to see a check pass.

item.description:
A verified KYC is needed to **apply to jobs** (admin rule "Karigars must be verified to apply", on by default). The PAN is checked against the Income Tax record on submit and Aadhaar is verified through **DigiLocker**. When both pass and the names agree, the KYC comes back `verified` straight away.

Flow:
1. **Start DigiLocker**, then open `authorization_url` in an in-app browser.
2. When the browser URL starts with `return_url_prefix`, close it.
3. **DigiLocker result** says `status: passed`.
4. **Submit KYC (PAN only, after DigiLocker)** answers `kyc.status: verified`.

No DigiLocker? **Submit KYC** with the Aadhaar number goes to admin review.

The saved examples were recorded against a test registry. The numbers in the bodies are placeholders, so the real registry answers `422 "not found"` to them: use real numbers to see a check pass.

Spec: docs/kyc-verification-decentro.md

`verification` says whether the karigar can apply (`can_apply`, `message`). `features.verification_required_to_apply` and `features.auto_verification_enabled` drive the KYC prompts.

item.name: Legal & Support (public)
item.description: Terms & Privacy and Help & Support. No token needed - the OTP screen links to the legal documents before an account exists, and someone who cannot sign in still needs help.

request.description: Both documents without their bodies, for the settings row. `web_url` is the same text as a web page for an "open in browser" link - it is null for the terms (no web page yet), so handle null. `updated_label` is pre-formatted; `updated_at` is for comparing.

The full document as sections of blocks. Exactly three block types: `paragraph` and `heading` carry `text`, `list` carries `items`. `heading` is a sub-heading inside a section - render it smaller than the section title and keep it out of the contents rail (build that from sections[].title / sections[].id). The identity-document section disappears when an admin switches verification off, so build the screen from what you get.
Same shape as the privacy policy. Any document key other than `terms` or `privacy` returns 404.

FAQs plus the ways to reach a person. A channel that is not configured is left out entirely - do not render a row for a missing key. `whatsapp` is digits with country code and no "+", so the app builds its own wa.me link. Pass `audience` (worker|employer) to get your app's entries plus the shared ones; omit it for all. Anything else returns 422. `id` is stable, so a single answer can be deep-linked.
